//: What the active character holds, wears and carries: everything inside it, each container before what it holds, indented under it, with how each is held and how full each container is; and its body as a tree of the parts on the outside, with what is worn over each. Enter on a thing opens `item`, the verbs that apply to it. All of it is the character's own (`view.carried`, `view.parts`, `view.worn_on`), and things are named in the reader's terms (`name`). Opened in play by the control `inventory` (i).
title: Inventory

list.item: {if it.holder == view then '' else '  '}{name(it)}{if (it.count ?? 1) > 1 then ' x' + str(it.count) else ''}  <dim>{if it.hold == 'grasp' then 'in hand' else if it.hold == 'worn' then 'worn' else if it.hold == 'stowed' or it.hold == 'inside' then 'in ' + name(it.holder) else if it.hold == 'fixed' then 'fitted to ' + name(it.holder) else ''}{if is_null(it.capacity_mass) then '' else ', ' + str(round((it.carried_mass ?? 0) * 10) / 10) + ' of ' + str(it.capacity_mass) + ' kg'}</>
list.tip: Enter: what to do with it.

tree.rows: if len(view.parts ?? []) == 0 or not is_null(view.parts[0].parent) then view.parts else [view.parts[0]]
tree.tip: Right opens a part, Left closes it.

tooltip.value: Enter on a thing: what to do with it. Tab: the other side. Esc: back.

//: What can be done with one thing the character has: the item actions, each named bare as the walking controls name `step`, with the thing as `what`: `drop`, `wear`, `take_off`, `stow`, `put_in` (which asks which container first and gives it as `container`), `take_out` and `give` (which asks to whom). The `core` mod defines them (`holding.json`); an action no loaded mod defines is refused by the simulation with its reason, which the log shows, and so is one that cannot be done, with the action's own reason. Opened by the inventory with the thing (`item`), how it is held (`hold`) and what it is called (`name`).
title: What to do

rows.text: <dim>Up and Down choose, Enter does it, Esc goes back.</>
